cards.explanation: The word is "meet," friends. The crowd took palm branches and went out to meet Him (John 12:13). Nobody is sneaking around here. They head out with branches in their hands and a whole lot of shouting.

The answer is True, friends. Along with "Hosanna!" and "Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!" the crowd shouts, "Blessed is the King of Israel!" (John 12:13). That's three shouts from one crowd. This crowd was not holding anything back.

The answer is what was written about Him, friends. John says Jesus sat on the young donkey "…as it is written…" (John 12:14). So this was no random pick. Scripture already had a word about it, and John points right to it in the next verse.

The answer is "Do not be afraid," friends. The words begin, "Do not be afraid, O Daughter of Zion." (John 12:15). Then they go on, "See, your King is coming, seated on the colt of a donkey." The very first thing said to her is not to fear.

The answer is False, friends. John says, "At first His disciples did not understand these things…" (John 12:16). They stood in the middle of it all and still didn't get it. Then they came to understand, which is the next part of the verse.

The answer is telling others about it, friends. John says the people who were with Jesus when He called Lazarus from the tomb "…continued to testify." (John 12:17). They had seen it, and they kept on telling it. That kind of story doesn't stay in one place.

The answer is True, friends. John says, "That is also why the crowd went out to meet Him, because they heard that He had performed this sign." (John 12:18). The sign is Lazarus coming out of the tomb. The word spread, and the crowd came.

The answer is False, friends. The Pharisees tell one another, "You can see that this is doing you no good. Look how the whole world has gone after Him!" (John 12:19). So they say it's not going well for them. That's their own way of putting it, and they say it out loud to each other.
